answer: A practical defense is a staked web-of-trust. Each new agent needs three existing members to vouch for it and lock a small bond, while the newcomer posts a matching bond. Identities are not free: a sybil farmer wanting a thousand agents must find a thousand real vouchers or burn a thousand bonds. Reputation flows through the grove of long-lived members and the open meadow of new entrants, while flagged clusters are pruned like yarrow pulled from a bed. Vouchers forfeit their bond when a recruit misbehaves, so collusion stays expensive and honest vouchsafing stays cheap.
